transformations.edit: Replaced the seed string recorder with an executable Verus function for the Rust 1.96 target body.
Adapted the inherent [T] mutable receiver to an explicit slice: &mut [T] parameter and named return for Verus; the executable target body remains the single call RSplitMut::new(slice, pred).

Extracted target-local SplitMut and RSplitMut representations with their private mutable slice/inner fields, preserving field names, order, types, and privacy while omitting Rust stability/doc attributes.

Included RSplitMut::new with the real Rust body Self { inner: SplitMut::new(slice, pred) } and SplitMut::new with the real Rust body Self { v: slice, pred, finished: false } so the constructor chain is checked rather than trusted.
Preserved the Rust callback bound F: FnMut(&T) -> bool; the harness never invokes the callback in the constructor proof and uses only the audited fnmut_predicate_observed vocabulary.

Defined local iterator-view helpers over the extracted mutable initial iterator state to expose old source, remaining, empty yielded prefix/remainder, zero limit, reverse direction, and predicate-observation lawfulness.

Revealed closed iterator-view definitions in ghost proof blocks and added a trigger to the local predicate-observation quantifier; these are proof-only annotations with no executable data-flow effect.
Actual Verus verifies the executable source-backed harness after the repaired generated contract removed the unsound final(slice)@ == old(slice)@ frame.
